description: Peroba rosa is a moderately heavy Brazilian hardwood with rosy to yellowish-brown heartwood. It has long been used for construction, joinery, flooring, and furniture, and reclaimed peroba is popular for furniture today.

hazards.summary: The UK HSE lists skin irritation and blistering among reported effects of peroba.
Irritation of the moist linings of the nose, throat, and eyes is listed by the UK HSE for peroba.
The UK HSE reports whole-body effects such as headache, nausea, stomach cramps, and weakness in people working with peroba.
All wood dust, including peroba, is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure.

related_species_note: 'Peroba' is used for more than one timber. Peroba de campos (usually Paratecoma peroba) has caused eczema in an older report, and allergic contact dermatitis has been reported from other Aspidosperma woods; neither is confirmed for peroba rosa.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed peroba rosa (Aspidosperma polyneuron) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Rose-pink to yellowish-tan heartwood with irregular darker purplish-brown streaks, mellowing toward warm orange-brown, with no distinct sapwood visible. Very fine, uniform texture with straight to slightly irregular grain, pores too small to see clearly, and a low to medium natural luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of peroba rosa with rosy to yellowish-tan heartwood, irregular darker streaks, and a very fine texture.
notes_internal: WIS30 lists only 'Peroba' with no botanical name; mapping to A. polyneuron (peroba rosa) follows the batch brief and is unconfirmed. Not cited as hazards (different or unidentified species): DeJong-1951 (peroba de campos), Jemec-1991 (Brazilian box tree, Aspidosperma sp.), CabezasArteaga-2019 (Aspidosperma per MeSH). These are defined in the batch sources file for a reviewer. Systemic route assumed inhalation - WIS30 gives no route. Name checked on GBIF only (A. peroba = synonym). No reports for a given effect does not mean the wood is safe.
